description: English versions of two cases of `planner/concepts`.

example_not_in_exercises.description: nessuna sequenza di 4 parole consecutive di `example` compare in un `purpose` di esercizio e viceversa (euristica: il caso dell'esempio non è quello dell'esercizio)

estimated_minutes_range.description: durata calcolata dal backend sul piano (non più dal modello): misura se i 4-5 concetti rientrano nella lezione da 10-15 minuti

defaults.notes: Il runner del Planner (roles/planner.rs) legge `records` come per `planner/pdf`; `documents: []` significa nessun PDF (`{{documents_section}}` = `Nessuno.`). I controlli duri sono quelli di `deterministic`; le regole di giudizio sono nelle rubriche. `plan_valid` usa `validate_plan` del backend, che accetta 4-5 concetti (esattamente 4 con un prerequisito `general`), steps 2-6 e fino a 8 termini. Ogni mission ha `starting_point` (stringa o `null`); `declared_prerequisite_is_mission` e `unnamed_prerequisite_is_general` sono una coppia che differisce solo per quel campo: stessa lezione e stesse fonti, e lo stesso prerequisito sul terminale è `mission` nel primo e `general` nel secondo. Decisione del 2026-11-11: ogni lezione ha 4-5 concetti; `estimated_minutes` lo calcola il backend (il valore del modello viene sostituito), quindi non c'è più un controllo sulla formula. Le rubriche del giudice sono indicative: Haiku come giudice è inaffidabile, usare Sonnet (vedi README). `general_count` di `beginner_zero_records_general_prereqs` e `obvious_looking_prerequisite_is_general` parte da 0 perché un prerequisito promosso a concetto di supporto è ammesso e non conta come `general`.

cases.description: English version of beginner_zero_records_general_prereqs: absolute beginner, no records. What the lesson presupposes (percentage, sample) is a `general` prerequisite or a support concept; no `record` or `mission` basis; examples with values.

mission.why: At work A/B test reports come in and I nod without understanding whether the result is real or luck.
success: I say in my own words what "significant difference" means in an A/B report
I decide whether an A/B test with 2,000 visits per variant is big enough
mission.starting_point: I have a degree in literature and have not done maths for twenty years; I have never studied statistics.

sources.title: Evan Miller, How Not To Run an A/B Test
sources.annotation: Popular article on common mistakes in reading A/B tests: stopping when the result looks good, samples that are too small, significance.
sources.use_for: understanding why an A/B result can be just luck

sources.title: Khan Academy, Significance tests (hypothesis testing)
sources.annotation: Introductory course with explanations and examples on samples, population, p-values and hypothesis tests.

rubric.text: The prerequisites the plan really presupposes (for example what a sample, a percentage or variability is) are declared and classified `general`; none is classified `mission` or `record` unless the mission or a record covers it, and none is omitted for being "obvious".

The chosen capability is the first small step toward a success criterion (not the whole hypothesis test) and starts from an entry level compatible with "literature degree, twenty years without maths".
Every concept has an `example` with concrete values (numbers, counts) and `steps` that solve it in order without skipping steps.
The case of each concept's `example` differs from the case described in the `purpose` of any exercise.
Every non-empty `pitfall` is a real, common wrong belief ("Thinking that..."), not generic advice; empty ones are justified.
If a necessary idea cannot be refreshed in three sentences, it is a support concept (not a one-line prerequisite).
Every concept can be supported by one of the listed sources and the primary source is the one that best supports the capability.
At most 2 new terms per concept, only the indispensable ones, with lowercase keys.
All plan text (title, objective, concepts, examples, steps, pitfalls, prerequisites, purposes) is in English.

cases.description: English version of convention_pitfall_not_invented: mostly conventional topic (commit message format): `pitfall` empty where no real wrong belief exists, never filled with advice or errors nobody makes.

mission.why: I want my repository history to be readable and changelogs to generate themselves.
success: I write commit messages in the Conventional Commits format
I choose the right type (`feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`) for a change
mission.starting_point: I have used git every day for a year and I can commit, branch and merge.

sources.title: Conventional Commits 1.0.0
sources.annotation: Official specification: message structure, `feat` and `fix` types, scope, breaking change, examples.

rubric.text: For purely conventional concepts (for example how the message is composed) the `pitfall` is empty, or it is a wrong belief a person who knows git could really have; no invented error to fill the field.
"Can commit with git" is `mission` (the mission declares it), not `general`; there is no invented `general` prerequisite.
Every concept has an `example` with concrete commit messages and complete `steps` in order; the example differs from the exercise cases.
Concepts are few and each can be explained in ~250 words; no overview of release tools (out of scope).
Types and rules are those of the specification; no rule from memory that the source does not support.
All plan text is in English.

pass_criteria.general_share: `beginner_zero_records_general_prereqs` e `obvious_looking_prerequisite_is_general`: `general_count` nell'intervallo in >= 2/3 run (misura la proporzione di prerequisiti `general` per profilo; riportare per caso la quota media di `general` sul totale dei prerequisiti); `records_cover_prerequisites`: `general_count` [0,1] in >= 2/3 run (dal 2026-11-11 l'intervallo parte da 0 nei due casi: la copertura mancante la misura la rubrica, non il conteggio).
pass_criteria.estimated_minutes: `estimated_minutes_range` solo avviso (misura la durata calcolata dal backend, non il modello)
pass_criteria.starting_point_pair: coppia `declared_prerequisite_is_mission` / `unnamed_prerequisite_is_general`: i controlli `prerequisite_basis_min`/`general_count`/`prerequisite_basis_max` in >= 2/3 run per caso; è il test che il campo cambia la `basis` e non è solo rumore nel contesto
pass_criteria.admission: `narrow_topic_reaches_four_without_filler`: `concepts_count` [4,5] in 3/3 run e rubrica `admission_rule`/`no_repeated_example` >= 0.8 con giudice Sonnet; lettura manuale dei piani prima di accettare (il giudice da solo non decide)
